dispatch_note: CUDA picks gather_qmv only when M*B < 8. A decode step routes 8 experts, so the model's own path is qmm_naive.
evidence: benchmarks/maple_qmm_naive_repro.py: every column of up_gate (1024) and down (2048), 4 experts x 2 layers, array_equal against the B=8 qmm_naive dispatch on layers 3 and 7; 0/4 against gather_qmv, which is a different kernel (the B=1 dispatch) and explains the earlier 51-58% figures.
finding: The stock decode MoE matmul (gather_qmm with 8 experts dispatches to qmm_naive on CUDA) is reproducible bit for bit inside an mx.fast.cuda_kernel: dequant as bf16(bf16(q*s)+z), the same mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k16.row.col.f32.bf16.bf16.f32 atom with row 0 of A populated, k-tiles of 128 accumulated in order, one bf16 epilogue rounding.
implication: Each output column depends only on the k-order, so any grid over columns preserves bits: an array-exact expert phase inside the megakernel is constructively possible. Remaining for a fully exact fast lane: router bits (softmax/top-8/renorm), bf16 activation rounding between the projections, and the stock aggregation order.
name: qmm_naive_bit_exact_reproduction

consequence: Every component of the MoE block now has a proven or nearly-proven bit recipe: an exact megakernel (megakernel speed, strict-lane stream) is an assembly task, not a research question.

purpose: Pin the bit-level reduction order of every stock op an array-exact fast lane must reproduce, beyond the expert matmuls already proven in maple_qmm_naive_repro.py.

aggregation_resolution: sum(axis=-2) over 8 experts dispatches to col_reduce_small: a plain linear loop. The failing detail was fma contraction -- the stock chain rounds the fp32 multiply in its own kernel before the sum ever sees it, so the recipe is __fmul_rn then __fadd_rn, never fmaf. Both 'obvious' candidates (contracted linear, explicit fmaf) hit 14/16; the butterfly guess from col_reduce_looped hit 53/64; the uncontracted linear loop hits 128/128.
status: Every component of the stock MoE block now has a hardware-proven bit recipe. The exact megakernel is an assembly task.

verdict: the sm90 regression is CPU-class, not grid starvation: on a starved host the lane WINS +13-14% at every grid (it removes host work), on a healthy-CPU host it loses ~12%; grids 64/96/128 tie within noise, 128 grazes the residency edge (the kernel's register weight holds ~one 1024-thread block per SM even on Hopper), 192 deadlock-spins. Auto default for sm90 stays OFF (healthy hosts are the norm); MAPLE_ATTENTION_MEGAKERNEL=1 is the documented lever for CPU-poor deployments; the grid override ceiling is cut to 112 everywhere above sm86
